title: Despair, the closed door
hook: no one despairs of Allah's mercy except those without faith (12:87)

segments.voice: Yesterday, ghaflah, heedlessness, and your line: wake up. When your reminder went off, what were you in the middle of? Day one thousand two hundred ninety.

A father at home, waiting. In Surah Yusuf, Jacob has lost his son Joseph, and now a second son is held far away in Egypt. The Qur'an says his eyes went white with grief. If anyone has a reason to close the door, it's him. And instead he turns to his other sons and sends them back out on the road: go, look for news of Joseph and his brother. Then he says the line this day is built on. Today: despair, the closed door.
screen: `A GRIEVING FATHER.` → `EYES WHITE WITH SORROW.` → `GO, LOOK FOR NEWS.`

segments.voice: Here is what Jacob says, in Pickthall's words: "despair not of the Spirit of Allah. Lo! none despaireth of the Spirit of Allah save disbelieving folk." First, notice who is speaking. This isn't someone with a comfortable life handing out advice. It's a man whose grief has taken his sight, telling his sons to keep looking. Hope, in this story, isn't a mood. It's an instruction to get back on the road. Second, despair is called a disease of the heart because of what it claims. It says: this is beyond Allah's mercy. That's a claim about Allah, and in the verse it sits next to unbelief. Third, a verse first met on the day of fear and hope, which opens the door wider still. In Pickthall's words: "Say: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins." Prodigal to their own hurt: people who have wasted a great deal, on themselves. The verse is addressed to them by name. And last, a look back. This part of the path began with a lump of flesh, the heart, and went through its diseases: arrogance, envy, showing off, anger, greed, backbiting, lying, heedlessness, and now despair. Every one of them had a cure: a correction accepted, a prayer, a hidden deed, a seat, enough, silence, a true sentence, a reminder. Despair says none of it will work. The verse says the door stays open.
screen: `DESPAIR NOT OF THE SPIRIT OF ALLAH.` · `A CLAIM ABOUT ALLAH'S MERCY.` · `PRODIGAL TO THEIR OWN HURT.` · then, large: `THE DOOR STAYS OPEN.`

segments.voice: The practice: hope in one hard thing. Settle, and breathe. Let one hard thing come to mind. Not everything; one. A relationship, a habit, a diagnosis, a debt, something you've decided won't change. Hold it the way Jacob held his lost son: honestly, without pretending it doesn't hurt. Then do what he did. Send someone back out on the road. What is one small step of looking, one question, one call, one try? If you pray, you can ask Allah for help with it by name. If not, just leave the door open a crack. The bell holds the time.
Despair. Giving up hope of Allah's mercy; in Surah Yusuf, the closed door a grieving father refuses to close. Today's word.

Your line: never despair. Take the one small step of looking you chose, today. That closes the diseases of the heart. Tomorrow begins the manners of daily life, with what adab means. Day one thousand two hundred ninety.

howItsDone: Muslim teachers treat despair of Allah's mercy as a disease of the heart, citing Jacob's words in Surah Yusuf and the call of Qur'an 39:53 to those who have wronged themselves not to despair.

fork.setup: you're Jacob. one son lost, another held in Egypt, your eyes gone white with grief. your other sons are in front of you. what do you do?
options: send them back out to look for news of Joseph and his brother.
go to Egypt yourself to fight.

original.note: Arabic: mercy; in 39:53, despair is despair of Allah's rahmah.

trapdoor: what you thought: despair is just a low mood.
what it means: in the Qur'an, despairing of Allah's mercy is a claim that something is beyond it, and the text refuses that claim.
what a scholar hears: Jacob's words in 12:87, set beside his grief in 12:84, and the wide address of 39:53 to those who wronged themselves.
